```lean
import Mathlib

variable {R M : Type*} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
  [Module.Free R M] {f : Module.End R M} 

-- Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.Basic
theorem Module.End.mem_center_iff :
    f ∈ Set.center (End R M) ↔ ∃ α ∈ Set.center R, ∀ x : M, f x = α • x := by
  simp only [Semigroup.mem_center_iff, LinearMap.ext_iff, mul_apply]
  refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, by simp_all⟩
  by_cases! Subsingleton M
  · exact ⟨0, by simp, fun _ ↦ Subsingleton.allEq _ _⟩
  let b := Free.chooseBasis R M
  let i := b.index_nonempty.some
  have (x : M) := by simpa using h ((b.coord i).smulRight x) (b i) |>.symm
  exact ⟨b.coord i (f (b i)),
    fun r ↦ by simpa using congr(b.coord i $(this (r • b i))), this⟩

-- Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.Basic
theorem Module.End.mem_submonoidCenter_iff :
    f ∈ Submonoid.center (End R M) ↔
      ∃ α ∈ Submonoid.center R, ∀ x : M, f x = α • x :=
  Module.End.mem_center_iff

-- Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FreeModule.Basic
theorem Module.End.mem_subsemigroupCenter_iff :
    f ∈ Subsemigroup.center (End R M) ↔
      ∃ α ∈ Subsemigroup.center R, ∀ x : M, f x = α • x :=
  Module.End.mem_center_iff

-- Mathlib.Algebra.Central.End
theorem Module.End.mem_subsemiringCenter_iff :
    f ∈ Subsemiring.center (End R M) ↔
      ∃ α ∈ Subsemiring.center R, ∀ x : M, f x = α • x :=
  Module.End.mem_center_iff

variable {S : Type*} [CommSemiring S] [Module S M]
  [SMulCommClass R S M] [Algebra S R] [IsScalarTower S R M]

-- Mathlib.Algebra.Central.End
theorem Module.End.mem_subalgebraCenter_iff :
    f ∈ Subalgebra.center S (End R M) ↔
      ∃ α ∈ Subalgebra.center S R, ∀ x : M, f x = α • x :=
  Module.End.mem_center_iff

attribute [-instance] Algebra.IsCentral.instEnd in
example [Algebra.IsCentral S R] : Algebra.IsCentral S (Module.End R M) where
  out x hT :=
    have ⟨α, h⟩ := Module.End.mem_subalgebraCenter_iff.mp hT
    have ⟨y, hy⟩ := Algebra.IsCentral.center_eq_bot S R ▸ h.1
    ⟨y, by aesop⟩
```

source_comments.author: robin-carlier
source_comments.body:
I feel like this proof is too specialized for the homotopy category. Mathlib arleady knows that quotient categories of categories with unique objects and subsingleton homs have subsingleton homs, and that free categories on quivers with unique objects and unique homs have unique homs, 
so by adding
```lean
instance (V : Type*) [ReflQuiver V] [Unique V]
    [∀ (x y : V), Subsingleton (x ⟶ y)] (x y : FreeRefl V) :
    Subsingleton (x ⟶ y) :=
  letI (x y : V) : Unique (x ⟶ y) := by
    obtain rfl : x = y := by subsingleton
    exact (unique_iff_subsingleton_and_nonempty _ |>.mpr ⟨inferInstance, ⟨𝟙rq _⟩⟩).some
  inferInstance
```
around line 312 in `CategoryTheory/Category/ReflQuiv.lean`, and
```lean
instance [Subsingleton (X _⦋1⦌₂)] {x y : X _⦋0⦌₂} : Subsingleton (X.Edge x y) where
  allEq f g := by
    ext
    subsingleton
```

somewhere in `AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/CompStructTruncated.lean`, 

this becomes
```lean
instance subsingleton_hom (X : Truncated.{u} 2) [Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂)] [Subsingleton (X _⦋1⦌₂)]
    (x y : X.HomotopyCategory) :
    Subsingleton (x ⟶ y) :=
  letI : Unique (OneTruncation₂ X) := inferInstanceAs (Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂))
  letI (x y : (OneTruncation₂ X)) : Subsingleton (x ⟶ y) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton <| X.Edge _ _)
  CategoryTheory.Quotient.instSubsingletonHom _ _ _
```
which is IMO the "morally correct" proof (arguably, we could even consider registering the instances for OneTruncation on their own, but I’m not sure that would be very useful).

Same here: we already have `Cat.isTerminalOfUniqueOfIsDiscrete`:
```suggestion
instance (X : Truncated.{u} 2) [Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂)] : Unique X.HomotopyCategory := 
  letI : Unique (OneTruncation₂ X) := inferInstanceAs (Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂))
  CategoryTheory.Quotient.instUnique _

/-- If `X : Truncated 2` has a unique `0`-simplex and (at most) one `1`-simplex,
then `X.HomotopyCategory` is a terminal object in `Cat`. -/

    IsTerminal (Cat.of X.HomotopyCategory) :=
  letI : IsDiscrete (X.HomotopyCategory) := { eq_of_hom := by subsingleton }
  Cat.isTerminalOfUniqueOfIsDiscrete
```

pr_summary: This PR extends the API around `ArchimedeanClass.stdPart` in `Algebra/Order/Ring/StandardPart.lean`, adding more simp/compatibility lemmas for how `stdPart` interacts with ring operations (notably `theorem stdPart_neg (x : K) : stdPart (-x) = -stdPart x`) and cleaning up proofs involving `mk_inv`/`stdPart_of_mk_ne_zero` in the inversion lemmas. It also tweaks the `FiniteElement` interface by adjusting/using `FiniteElement.mk` and makes a couple of small proof refactors elsewhere (including using `mk_map_of_archimedean' ⟨Int.castRingHom S, …⟩ h` in `Algebra/Order/Ring/Archimedean.lean`). Structurally, most changes are proof-level rewrites (`simp_rw`, `rwa`, `congr` + `Subsingleton.allEq`) rather than new definitions, aiming to make existing lemmas easier to apply by simp.

pr_summary: This PR is a library refactor in Analysis (and a few adjacent files) whose goal is to standardize the “multiply by a scalar” continuous linear map: it rewrites occurrences of `smulRight (1 : R →L[R] R)` (or `smulRight (.id R R)`) in definitions/lemmas to the dedicated map `toSpanSingleton R`. It does not introduce new mathematics, but changes many statements/definitions in calculus/derivative-related files (and some Fourier/measure/manifold lemmas) to use the preferred name, relying on the existing lemma `ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_one_eq_toSpanSingleton`. Unusually, it deliberately avoids making that lemma a `[simp]` lemma because Geometry still has definitions and simp theorems phrased with `smulRight (1 : ...)`, so the PR is a targeted rewrite rather than a global simp-normalization.
